question_text: A developer runs initiate-auth with USER_PASSWORD_AUTH and receives: NotAuthorizedException: Client configured with secret but SECRET_HASH was not received. What is the root cause and fix?

options.text: The Cognito app client was created as a confidential client with a client secret — fix by creating a public app client without a client secret
The user has not confirmed their email

explanation: When a Cognito app client has a client secret (confidential client), every auth request must include a SECRET_HASH (HMAC-SHA256). Standard CLI and frontend SDKs do not compute this. The fix: create a new app client with the client secret toggle disabled (public client). Incorrect passwords produce 'Incorrect username or password'; disabled auth flow and unconfirmed users produce different errors.
source_topic: Cognito SECRET_HASH NotAuthorizedException on confidential client

topic: KMS CMK PendingDeletion blocks snapshot restore
question_text: A developer deletes the customer-managed KMS key that encrypted an Aurora Serverless v2 cluster. The cluster's automated snapshots still exist. What happens when they try to restore from a snapshot?

options.text: Restoration fails — the KMS key enters PendingDeletion (7-30 days) and encrypted snapshots cannot be decrypted
Snapshots are automatically re-encrypted with an AWS-managed key
Snapshots are deleted when the key is deleted
Restoration proceeds normally using the default aws/rds key

explanation: When you schedule deletion of a customer-managed KMS key, it enters PendingDeletion for 7-30 days. During and after this period, encrypted snapshots cannot be restored because the decryption key is unavailable. AWS does not re-encrypt snapshots with a different key, nor are they automatically deleted with the key. This is why development/test clusters should prefer the AWS-managed key (alias/aws/rds).
source_topic: KMS CMK PendingDeletion prevents snapshot restoration
